target_customer: Teams and knowledge workers running meetings (freemium web app with premium tier)
problem: Meetings waste time; teams lack habits around agendas, staying on track and following up on next steps.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with premium features (custom templates, team task viewer)

founders.name: Val Agostino
founders.background_notes: Later co-founder/CEO of Monarch Money per YC bio

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard web app for agendas, timers and action items; small team of 2.

defensibility.rationale: Easily copied feature set; no network effects or integrations described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cisco bought the team in October 2016 for an undisclosed sum, folded it into Spark as Meeting Notes, and made the product free.

market_need_then: Company cited roughly 3 billion US meetings a year with about half the time wasted; this is the company's own claim.
outcome_analysis: WorkLife was a small two to three person meeting-productivity app that raised only a little over one million dollars according to Crunchbase as reported by TechCrunch, and was bought by Cisco in October 2016 about two years after launch. Cisco absorbed the team into Spark and made the product free, which looks like a soft-landing talent deal rather than a scaled outcome; price was undisclosed.
notes: Total raised just over $1M per Crunchbase via TechCrunch; round dates, investors unknown, so no rounds recorded. Acquihire classification is an inference from team-into-Spark and free product; deal terms undisclosed. Founder bio details only for Agostino.
